narration.text: Why auroras glow about 100 kilometres above you.
None have been found below 70 kilometres.
Solar particles excite oxygen atoms high in the air.
Lower down, oxygen glows green at 557.7 nanometres.
Higher up, it glows red at 630 nanometres.
Airliners cruise far below, around 10 kilometres up.
So the northern lights happen at the edge of space.
